newsitem.title: USA: Russians wrote atomic history for U.S. - report.
newsitem.headline: Russians wrote atomic history for U.S. - report.

text.p: Within a year of the Soviet Union's collapse, a group of Russia's top atomic weapons scientists agreed to write and sell to the United States a massive, secret study of the history of Soviet nuclear weapons testing, the Washington Post reported on Sunday.
The newspaper, quoting documents and interviews with key Russian participants, said the deal provided first-hand information about Cold War events stretching over more than four decades.
The history project, which was led by Alexander Tchernyshev, a theoretical physicist at Arzamas-16, Russia's first nuclear weapons laboratory, remained shrouded in secrecy, the report said.

But the scope of the project -- a detailed 2,000-page history of 715 Soviet nuclear tests over 41 years -- was unprecedented and appeared to have given the United States valuable insights into Soviet military and scientific procedures, according to the Post.
It could also help American monitoring of any future nuclear explosions by rogue states that defy a new ban.
Starting in December 1992, Tchernyshev and about 200 other scientists wrote the history under contract to the U.S. Defence Special Weapons Agency for a fee of $288,501, the report said.
At the time, the scientists were suffering economically and the United States was trying to prevent them from taking their nuclear weapons expertise elsewhere.
The information the scientists provided was the objective of a costly monitoring effort by the United States during the Cold War using the U-2 spy plane as well as balloons and satellites.
The Post said by filling in the gaps the history would help the Pentagon better understand Russian procedures and adjust its systems to allow better monitoring of tests in the future.

Tchernyshev told the Post the Russian scientists did not divulge state secrets. He acknowledged that the information given to the United States was "sensitive" but was screened by a Russian declassification process "and we have the documents to prove it."
